text:
ana: quick a11y check on the new Filters drawer before we ship the dashboard tweak tomorrow AM. Main things: chip keyboard nav, focus ring contrast in dark mode, and screen-reader labeling for the search-combobox. Screenshot + prototype: https://img.redwood.ai/UX/filters-drawer.png

Tom: first pass — when I tab into the chip row focus lands on the first chip but arrow keys don't move focus, you have to Tab again. That's not a good keyboard pattern for a chip list. Recommend roving tabindex or role="listbox" with `aria-activedescendant`.

kevin: saw the same. Also the focus outline in dark theme is pretty faint (token `--focus-subtle`). Contrast measurements around 2.4:1. Needs at least 3:1 for non-text UI components per WCAG 2.1. Suggest `--focus-strong` or increase thickness.

maya: I'd prefer using native <button> for chips so screen readers announce "button" and we can use `aria-pressed` for toggled state. For multi-select chips use `aria-pressed="true"`. Example: 
```
<button class="chip" aria-pressed="false" aria-controls="results-list">Embeddings</button>
```

ellie: quick note: VoiceOver reads the combobox as "search, edit text" but doesn't expose the suggestion count. We should add `aria-expanded` and a live region announce like "3 suggestions" when the list opens. Also add an accessible name: `aria-label="Filter search"` if the visible label is icon-only.

sam: live updates: when filters change we update the results count at top of list. Currently every change triggers an aria-live update which floods SR users if someone drags a slider. Debounce updates and use `aria-atomic="true"` so it reads a single coherent sentence, e.g., "Filters applied. 1,234 results."

kevin: small implementation caveat: don't use aria-hidden on the visible count and a hidden live node simultaneously; that causes duplicates in some readers. Either update the visible node and make it live (`aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="true"`) or maintain a single offscreen live region.

Tom: motion nit: when a chip is toggled it briefly scales with a 200ms transform. Respect `prefers-reduced-motion` and either remove or switch to an opacity fade. CSS: `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .chip { transition: none; transform: none; } }`

maya: copy nit — the tooltip for the "Clear all" button reads "Clear filters (0)" on hover which reads oddly to SR users. Change to "Clear all filters" and add `aria-disabled="true"` when count is zero so it's announced as disabled.

ellie: compatibility check: NVDA+Firefox reads `aria-pressed` on buttons fine, but older TalkBack on Android had issues with `aria-activedescendant` patterns. If we go listbox+activedescendant, ensure we provide keyboard instructions in a help text and fallback focus model for mobile.

sam: ran local a11y-ci scan on branch `filters-drawer-v2`  found 3 issues: low focus contrast, missing aria-activedescendant for chip row (or alternative roving), and combobox missing aria-expanded updates. Full results: https://ci.redwood.ai/a11y/filters/2316004321

ana: (typo, meant ana) created quick tickets: UX-4030 (chip keyboard pattern + activedescendant fallback), UX-4031 (focus-ring contrast dark + token update), UX-4032 (combobox aria-expanded + suggestion count live announce), UX-4033 (clear-all button aria-disabled + copy). I'll link PRs and add QA checklist.

kevin: timeline? want to ship with canary but prefer the focus contrast fix in prod. If we can't get roving-tab done, we can ship with native buttons and a small keyboard hint in the drawer header and follow up with full activedescendant pattern.

Tom: agreed. I'll implement native button approach + aria-pressed today and file a follow-up for activedescendant.

maya: I'll update the tooltip copy and add the aria-disabled state in the same PR.

ellie: I'll run VoiceOver + TalkBack smoke tomorrow AM.

sam: I'll rerun a11y-ci after the PR and post results here. :thumbsup:
